title: Why we only see one side of the Moon

scenes.text: You have never seen the back of the Moon.
The Moon always shows us the same face.
Not because it doesn't spin. It spins exactly once per orbit, about every 27 days.
Long ago it spun faster, but Earth's gravity stretched it into a slight bulge.
Tugging on that bulge slowed its spin until it locked.
It's called tidal locking, and Earth's own spin is slowly slowing too.
